task_reconstruction.official_task: 2023 MCM Problem C, Wordle: the report count, the hard-mode share, the try distribution, and word difficulty.
required_outputs: a forecast interval for the report count
a decision on whether word attributes change the hard-mode share
a letter to the puzzle editor

writing_logic.summary: The trend is read off the figure before the test is named.
Two routes reach the same order, and the criterion only adjudicates.
The fit is a premise, and the sentence spends it on today's word.
The unexpected failure is reported before the choice.

contributions.summary: The report count is forecast with an interval and an expected value.
Today's word is separated from the words of the past days.
Data augmentation is shown to hurt, and feature engineering to help one model.
EERIE is placed in the second easiest of four groups.

models.summary: MU-C-Q258-001: a rolling mean and three standard deviations
MU-C-Q258-002: an ARIMA model reduced to one difference and one moving-average term
MU-C-Q258-003: a gradient-boosted tree on the current word and five lags
MU-C-Q258-004: seven separate boosted trees against a multi-gate mixture of experts
MU-C-Q258-005: a four-group K-means followed by a boosted-tree classifier

dependency_graph.label: The repaired series is the one the ARIMA model is fit to.
The repaired hard-mode share is the label of the boosted tree.
The same word attributes become the inputs of the two distribution models.
The try shares that the distribution model predicts are the features the clustering groups.

assumptions.summary: The Twitter reports stand for all players, and the hard-mode share matches.
The recorded distribution is completely accurate.
The seven shares have both correlations and differences.
Difficulty is proportional to the average number of tries.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Four outliers are replaced by linear interpolation, and the four-letter words are deleted.
Table 2 lists seven repairs, with adjusted numbers of 10.37, 9.48, 8.15, and 3.54 percent.
Every attribute is scaled to [0, 1] and the block is named Datainput.

results_trace.summary: March 31, 2023 falls in [10139.23, 30808.07] at 80 percent, and the expected value is 20473.65.
The hard-mode share has almost nothing to do with today's word.
EERIE belongs to the second category, at 71.13 percent validation accuracy.

verification.summary: The raw series has an ADF statistic of -1.9608 and a p-value of 0.5934.
ARIMA(0,1,1) has the smallest AIC, 4200.897, and the residual p-values are all above 0.05.
The validation accuracy is 71.13 percent, the precision 71.85, the recall 66.54, and the F1 69.09.

weaknesses.summary: The summary prints we attemptd, and a sensitivity analysis to the commission rate, a quantity the body never defines.
Section 4.4 dates the forecast March 31, while the summary and the letter say March 1.
Equation (6) divides by n and sums to n_j.
The section heading prints Classfication, and Table 8 prints Traning set and Mesuring.
Reference [2] prints macroeconmic, and reference [7] prints A. B.and Kuperman.
The letter closes with wish Wordle become better and better.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The paper reports that augmentation made both models worse, which is a result a team might rather omit.
The letter rounds the interval and changes the date, so the reader of the letter cannot recover the body.

independent_extensions.summary: Reconcile the March 31 of section 4.4 with the March 1 of the summary and the letter.
Rewrite the center update so the denominator matches the number of points in the cluster.

unresolved_questions: Why does section 4.4 date the forecast March 31, 2023, when the summary and the letter say March 1?
Why does equation (6) divide by n while the sum runs to n_j?
What is the commission rate named in the summary, which the body never defines?
Why does the summary round the test accuracy to 70 percent when Table 8 prints 71.13?
Why does the letter print [10139, 30808] for the interval the body prints as [10139.23, 30808.07]?

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Report the failed attempt and say what it produced.
Establish the fit, then spend it on the question.
